key_insight: RareDxR1 is an end-to-end reasoning model for rare disease diagnosis that learns directly from unstructured clinical notes, aiming to overcome phenotype extraction and retrieval bottlenecks.
clinical_relevance: If validated in practice, this approach could help support faster and more complete differential diagnosis for patients with rare, hard-to-recognize conditions.
method: Internalizes fragmented rare-disease knowledge into model parameters instead of relying on predefined ontologies or RAG.
Uses Reflection-Enhanced Reasoning Sampling to learn from failed attempts and generate expert-like diagnostic trajectories without human annotation.
Applies dual-level curriculum reinforcement learning to progressively improve rare disease diagnostic reasoning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art accuracy across multiple benchmarks for open-domain rare disease diagnosis.
watch_item: Because the system is described from benchmark results in the abstract, real-world clinical reliability, generalizability, and safety still need careful prospective validation.
paper_title: RareDxR1: Autonomous Medical Reasoning for Rare Disease Diagnosis Beyond Human Annotation
